question: What was the contribution of the agriculture sector to the GDP in 1950?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.675**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 1950, the agriculture sector was the dominant sector in India's economy, contributing significantly to the GDP.
 
• The agriculture sector's contribution to GDP in 1950 was approximately **67.5%**.
 
• This high percentage indicates the agrarian nature of the Indian economy during the early years of independence.
 
• Agriculture provided employment to a large portion of the population and was a primary source of livelihood.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:**

 
 
• Started in the 1960s to increase agricultural production through high-yielding varieties, better irrigation, and modern techniques.
 
• It significantly boosted the production of staples such as wheat and rice.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Policies:**
 
 
• Post-independence, the Indian government focused on land reforms and improved agricultural practices.
 
• Policies aimed to increase productivity and self-sufficiency in food grains.
 
 
 
• **Economic Transition:**
 
 
• Over the decades, the contribution of agriculture to GDP has decreased as India transitioned to a more industrial and service-oriented economy.
 
• Despite this, agriculture remains a critical sector for employment and rural livelihoods.
 
 
 
• **Modern Agricultural Challenges:**
 
 
• Issues such as climate change, water scarcity, and land degradation are modern challenges faced by the agriculture sector.
 
• There is a growing emphasis on sustainable and climate-resilient agricultural practices.
